subtitle: The Verdant Ocean and the Whispering Woods of the western coast, where the Veridian Keepers keep the Shore of the First Cycle
canonNote: Canon (book3 ch.1-7, world_bible.md): the Verdant Shore, the 'Verdant Ocean' of the Western Coast, a forest 'that didn't know when to stop': giant trees with trunks as wide as houses, broad flat leaves that sway like a green tide, a thousand greens from obsidian moss to emerald-glowing new ferns (ch.1); the Ridge of Long Shadows, the basalt divide the survivors crest to see it, with a harbour at its foot (ch.1, 3); the Veridian Keepers, beings of living wood and moss, and Oak-Bane and Willow-Whisper (ch.2, world_bible.md); the Veridian Temple, a stair of calcified roots down to the Root-Mother (ch.7); Ghost-Oaks tapped for Veridian sap 'the color of liquid emerald' (ch.4); the Whispering Glade and the mossy outcrop over it (ch.5); glass-frogs (ch.2); the Salt-Flats (ch.3); and the mists below the ridge, where an unnatural violet fog that tastes of ozone brings the Void-Touchers and the Pale Shadows (ch.2-4, 8). The game is set before the books' exodus: the survivors, Elara's First Seed (the Veridian Pine), the Salt-Wall and Salt-Mender's Landing are not here yet, and the Pale's touch is shown early, as foreshadowing (PROVISIONAL). The mountains between the Rim and the Shore are Book 3's ash-mountains (book2 ch.26: the Ashlands of the lower North were once the forested Verdant Spine); the road over them is GAME-ONLY. GAME-ONLY: Rootfast and every Keeper but Oak-Bane and Willow-Whisper, Mossveil Falls, the Wending, the Mistmere, the Fern Hollow, the Fallen Ghost-Oak, the Antler Meadow, the Greying, Palemist Hollow (canon's 'mists below the ridge'), the creatures and camps, and all placement. The Root-Mother's Deep under the Temple (its root-stair, Sap Well, the cold in the root and the Hollow Root-Warden) is GAME-ONLY. The filled-out shore (2026-10-04): creeping briars in the Fern Hollow, spiders on the basalt shoulder of the Ridge of Long Shadows (CANON place), the Void-Touchers the violet fog brings below the ridge (CANON, shown early: PROVISIONAL), Old Brine-Tusk in the south-west wood, and their quests; all placement GAME-ONLY. The residents' and villagers' stories, and the secrets' clues and hints (2026-10-15), are GAME-ONLY lines about the canon things named here; the book of lore's two pages here are labelled on the page.
worldMapNote: Placed on the western coast of the game map, beyond the western mountains where Book 3's survivors come down to the sea; canon gives the Shore no spot on this chart, so the position is provisional.

landmarks.name: The Ridge of Long Shadows
landmarks.text: The last ridge of the ash-mountains. Behind you, black basalt under a grey sky; before you, green to the edge of the world.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Ridge of Long Shadows, the jagged divide where the fire-scorched basalt of the North gives way to the Verdant Shore (book3 ch.1, 3). Its shape and the road over it are GAME-ONLY.

landmarks.name: The Verdant Ocean
landmarks.text: A forest that didn't know when to stop: trunks as wide as houses, and broad leaves that move like a green tide, all the way to the sea.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Verdant Shore, the 'Verdant Ocean', and its look (book3 ch.1). The view from the ridge is the zone's first sight of it.

landmarks.name: Rootfast
landmarks.text: The Keepers' bower: houses grown into the roots of the oldest trees, and lanterns of sap that light gold-green at dusk.
landmarks.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: Rootfast, its treehouses and its lanterns. The Veridian Keepers, beings of living wood and moss who keep the Shore, are CANON (book3 ch.2, world_bible.md).

landmarks.name: The Veridian Temple
landmarks.text: White roots, calcified like old bone, arch over a stair that winds down into a green glow. Living roots have closed across it. Something below is breathing.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Veridian Temple, the root-nexus of the forest, reached down a stair of calcified roots, where the Root-Mother sleeps (book3 ch.2, 7, 10). Its mouth here is CANON-EXPANDED; it is not entered (canon has it found and entered later).

landmarks.name: Mossveil Falls
landmarks.text: Water out of the ridge itself, falling over moss into a pool so green it looks lit from below.
landmarks.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the falls and their name. The Shore's waters and the ridge are CANON (book3 ch.1).

landmarks.name: The Mistmere
landmarks.text: A lake that keeps its mist till noon, and some days past it. Reeds, and glass-frogs clicking to each other across the water.
landmarks.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the Mistmere. Glass-frogs in the undergrowth are CANON (book3 ch.2); Willow-Whisper guides the lost through the mists (world_bible.md).

landmarks.name: The Whispering Glade
landmarks.text: Caps that glow at dusk the colour of the sea in shallow water. Stand still long enough and the glade hums.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Whispering Glade and the moss-covered outcrop over it (book3 ch.5). Its glowing caps are CANON-EXPANDED (the forest's bioluminescence, book3 ch.4, 7).

landmarks.name: The Fern Hollow
landmarks.text: Ferns taller than a man close over your head. Down here the light is green and the air is wet.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: ferns as tall as men unfurling in the Verdant Ocean (book3 ch.2); the hollow is GAME-ONLY.

landmarks.name: The Fallen Ghost-Oak
landmarks.text: A Ghost-Oak fell here before anyone counted years. Its crown is a hill of dead wood now, and the spiders have hung it with silk.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Ghost-Oaks are the Shore's great sap-trees (book3 ch.4-6); this fallen one and its spiders are GAME-ONLY.

landmarks.name: The Salt-Flats
landmarks.text: Grey-white slush and salt-crust where the forest gives up at last, and past it the sound of the sea.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON: the Salt-Flats of the western coast (book3 ch.3). The tidal pools and the glass-ship scout's camp are GAME-ONLY.

landmarks.name: The Greying
landmarks.text: A stand of Ghost-Oaks gone grey from the heart out. The moss on them is dust, and nothing sings here.
landmarks.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the Greying, an early sign of the Pale's reach. The Pale Kings and their cold are CANON (book3 ch.2-8); the Pale touching the Shore before the exodus is PROVISIONAL foreshadowing.

landmarks.name: Palemist Hollow
landmarks.text: A hollow under the ridge where the fog never lifts. It is cold and dry in a wet wood, and it tastes of lightning.
landmarks.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the mists below the ridge where the Void-Touchers gather (book3 ch.2) and the unnatural violet fog that tastes of ozone and unmaking (book3 ch.3-4); the hollow, its name and this early sighting are GAME-ONLY.

residents.name: Willow-Whisper
residents.title: Voice of the Wood
stories: The Root-Mother dreamed this shore in the First Cycle, before your kind had words. We are what she dreamed to keep it. We sing so that she dreams well. Lately the dream has a cold in it.
There was a cycle before this one. It ended in cold. The trees remember it in their rings, if you know where to count. I know where to count.
One day people will come over the ridge with nothing, and ask. I have dreamed it. I do not know yet what I will answer. I would like to have practised on you.

residents.name: Moss-Lantern
residents.title: Keeper of the Lanterns
stories: A lantern is a little of the day, kept. The caps in the glade make their own. We only borrow it. Borrowing is the whole of the Keepers' law, and the whole of what your kind forgets.
I keep the lanterns on the ridge road lit for the ones who will come down it. None have come, yet. One lights a lantern for the coming, not the come.
Sap-cakes, warm from the stone. I learned the stone from Alder-Knot and the sap from asking. Two each, this once.

residents.name: Alder-Knot
residents.title: Bark-Carver
stories: Wood, bone and patience. Iron rusts on this shore in a season; the salt in the air sees to it. The glass-ship woman's boat is coming apart at every nail. I offered treenails. She is thinking about it.
I carved Thorn-Hand's staff before the Greying took him. A Keeper is grown from a heart that is still green. I am keeping a cutting. Do not tell Oak-Bane.
The briars hunt now. Briars did not hunt when I was a sapling. Something in the fog below the ridge has taught them. I would like to cut one open and see what.

residents.name: Reed-Song
residents.title: Keeper of the Mere
stories: The glass-frogs sing the mere's hours. When they stop along a line, something has walked that line. They have stopped from the hollow toward the mere, lately. I count the quiet every night.
The mere keeps its mist till noon. It is shy. It has been shy for a thousand years and I see no reason to hurry it.
A Keeper slept a hundred years under the ferns south of the grove, once, and the moss there still glows. That was my grandmother. Do not step on her.

residents.name: Oak-Bane
residents.title: Guardian of the Deep Wood
stories: I was grown to keep the deep wood. I have kept it eight hundred years. In eight hundred years nothing came through the briar way that I did not let through. You, I let through. Do not make me regret the exception.
The grey is in Greyheart's rings. A Keeper does not die. A Keeper is laid down. I have laid down four this season. I was grown to fight. There is nothing to fight.
The flesh-folk come for the sap. Always the sap. One of them asked first. I remember her. I remember all of them. That is the trouble with being a tree.

residents.name: Sister Iselle
residents.title: Silent Pilgrim
stories: The Original Song has three notes: Earth, Spirit, Silence. Elder Orym hears all three at once. I have heard two in this glade. The third is what the fog is made of, I think, and I would rather not hear it.
Brother Wystan came west with me to listen at the Temple. He went down the root-stair and did not come back up. The Archive will want his page. I want him.
We wear silver masks in the south so that our faces do not get in the way of listening. Here I have taken mine off. The wood already knows what I look like.

residents.name: Ondine Varro
residents.title: Glass-Ship Scout
stories: Port Caelum builds ships of glass, and the Trade Princes keep pleasure barges in the Gilded Bay. I scout coves for the former so I never have to crew the latter.
Veridian sap, the colour of liquid emerald. House Glass will pay a ship's worth for three flasks. The Keepers let it be taken a little at a time, by those who ask. I asked. I'm still asking.
A glass-ship put in under this ridge before my time and never sailed out. The log was never found. I'd give a year's pay to read it, and I'd not tell House Glass what it said.

secrets.name: Above Mossveil Falls
secrets.text: From the lip of the falls the Wending runs away west in long green loops, under trees as tall as towers, all the way to a line of white that must be the sea.
secrets.clue: Climb to the lip of the falls in the north-east. From there the river runs away west in green loops to a line of white that must be the sea.
secrets.hint: Moss-Lantern says the flesh-folk never climb to the lip of the falls, north-east of the grove. From there, she says, you can see the river all the way to the sea.
secrets.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: Mossveil Falls and this lookout. The Verdant Ocean running down to the sea is CANON (book3 ch.1).

secrets.name: The Mossy Outcrop
secrets.text: A shelf of mossy rock above the Whispering Glade. From up here the glowing caps below look like a second sky, and the glade's hum comes up through the moss into your hands.
secrets.clue: A shelf of mossy rock above the glade of the glowing caps in the north. From up there they look like a second sky.
secrets.hint: Sister Iselle says there's a shelf of rock above the glade to the north, and from it the caps below look like stars. The hum comes up through the moss, she says.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: a moss-covered outcrop overlooking the Whispering Glade (book3 ch.5); the lookout is GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: The Tapper's Stump
secrets.text: Somebody used this stump as a cupboard: a bone spout, a stoppered flask gone dry, and a pair of gloves stained green to the wrist. The Keepers let the sap be taken a little at a time, by those who ask.
secrets.clue: South-west, where the old Ghost-Oaks are tapped, somebody used a hollow stump as a cupboard: a bone spout, a dry flask, green-stained gloves.
secrets.hint: Alder-Knot says the sap-tapper before Ondine kept his tools in a hollow stump among the old Ghost-Oaks in the south-west. Gloves stained green to the wrist. He asked first, that one.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Ghost-Oaks tapped for Veridian sap, which must not get into a wound (book3 ch.4); the tapper, the custom and the gloves are GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: A Glass-Ship's Log
secrets.prompt: Work the oilcloth packet out from under the drift-log
secrets.text: Pushed under a bleached drift-log above the tide-line: an oilcloth packet with a few pages of a ship's log in it, the ink run but readable.
secrets.clue: On the salt shore in the far south-west, above the tide-line, an oilcloth packet is pushed under a bleached drift-log.
secrets.hint: Ondine Varro says a glass-ship put in under the ridge once and didn't leave by sea. Somebody kept the log dry under a drift-log above the tide-line, on the salt shore to the south-west.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Port Caelum and its glass ships (world_bible.md), the harbour below the ridge and the Salt-Flats (book3 ch.3) are CANON; the ship and its log are GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: Lantern-Moss
secrets.text: A cushion of moss that glows like a banked coal under the ferns, gold-green and warm to the touch. The Keepers say it grows where one of them once slept for a hundred years.
secrets.clue: Under the ferns south-east of the grove, a cushion of moss glows like a banked coal, warm to the touch. A Keeper slept there a hundred years.
secrets.hint: Reed-Song says a Keeper slept a hundred years under the ferns south-east of the grove, and the moss there still glows like a banked coal. Warm, if you put your hand on it.

secrets.name: A Pilgrim's Abandoned Pack
secrets.prompt: Search the pack by the sap-pool
secrets.text: A Silent Pilgrim's travelling pack, the straps chewed through, left by the sap-pool: a listening-tube of brass, bent, and a purse nobody came back for.
secrets.clue: By the sap-pool in the far north-west, a traveller's pack with its straps chewed through: a bent brass listening-tube in it, and a purse nobody came back for.
secrets.hint: Willow-Whisper says one of the silent ones laid down a pack by the sap-pool in the far north-west and did not pick it up again. The wood does not take such things. It only waits.
secrets.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the pack; the Silent Pilgrims are CANON.

secrets.name: The Lantern Count
secrets.prompt: Lift the bark from the moss
secrets.text: A shelf of bark laid on the moss at the outcrop's edge, cut with small, even strokes: Moss-Lantern's count of the lanterns, from the First Cycle to one she has not finished.
secrets.clue: On the shelf of mossy rock above the glade of the glowing caps in the north, a Keeper cut her count of the lanterns into a piece of bark.
secrets.hint: Moss-Lantern says she cut the count of the lanterns into bark and left it on the rock above the glade, in the north, for any flesh-folk who climb that high. Few do. She would like one to.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Root-Mother, the First Cycle and the Keepers' rule against hoarding are CANON (book3 ch.2, 6-7; world_bible.md); Moss-Lantern and her count are GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: Willow-Whisper's Leaf
secrets.prompt: Ease the strip of bark out of the moss
secrets.text: Pressed into the moss at the lip of the falls, kept green by the wood: a strip of pale bark in the Keepers' spiral-script, left for whoever climbs up here to look down, and for who comes after.
secrets.clue: At the lip of the falls in the north-east, pressed into the moss, a strip of pale bark in the Keepers' spiral-script waits for whoever climbs up to look down.
secrets.hint: Willow-Whisper says she left a leaf at the lip of the falls, north-east of the grove, for the ones who will come over the ridge one day. She says you may read it first, since you asked. She says you always ask. That is why.
secrets.canonStatus: PROVISIONAL foreshadowing within CANON: the Root-Mother, the river to the sea and the survivors who crest the Ridge of Long Shadows are CANON (book3 ch.1-4, 7); Willow-Whisper's leaf is GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: The Tale-Book on Its Stand
secrets.prompt: Read the book on the root-stand
secrets.text: A stand of grown root by the glade path, and on it a book the Keepers bring out of the Hearth-Tree at dusk to read to whoever sits: the tales of the bower, in a dozen hands.
secrets.clue: Between the guest-trees and the glowing caps, a stand of grown root holds a book the Keepers read aloud at dusk.
secrets.hint: Moss-Lantern says the tale-book sits on its root-stand by the path north of the hearth-tree, out of the rain. Read it by day, she says. At dusk somebody will read it to you, whether you like it or not.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Veridian Keepers and their bower are CANON (book3 ch.1-7); the book and its tales are GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: The Tide-Post
secrets.prompt: Look at the notches on the driftwood post
secrets.text: A driftwood post sunk in the salt-crust, notched up its side: one cut for every year the salt came further in, and a name by some of them. The Salt-Menders' count, older than the ships.
secrets.clue: Where the forest gives up at last and the ground is salt, a driftwood post counts the years the salt came further in.
secrets.hint: Ondine Varro says the Salt-Menders' tide-post stands out on the white ground west of here. A notch a year. She says the ships are younger than the notches, and that's the point of it.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: salt and the Salt-Menders are CANON (LORE_AUDIT.md: the game's are the forerunners of book 3's); the post and its count are GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: The Moss-Saint's Shrine
secrets.text: A wayshrine grown over with moss, its saint a carved Keeper with a lantern, and a dish of crowns that nobody here would take. Travellers leave one for the road west.
secrets.clue: East of where the caps glow at dusk, a little mossed shrine keeps a dish of crowns no Keeper would take.
secrets.hint: Sister Iselle says there's a little shrine east of the glowing caps, grown over with moss. Leave a crown, she says, for the road. She doesn't say which road.
secrets.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the shrine and its saint. The Veridian Keepers are CANON (book3 ch.1-7).

secrets.name: An Ore-Hunter in the Root
secrets.text: Against the root wall of the hall of columns: bones in rotten leathers, a pick across the knees, a sack of green ore he never carried out, and the green-bronze legplates he had made from his first haul. The root has grown over his boots.
secrets.clue: In the hall of root columns below the stair, someone came down for the green ore and sat against the wall with his sack full. The root has his boots.
secrets.hint: Oak-Bane says a man went down under the temple for the green ore two winters back, with a pick and a sack. He's still down there in the hall of root columns. The root has his boots now.
secrets.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the ore-hunter and his reckoning. The Root-Mother is CANON (book3); the cold in the root is PROVISIONAL foreshadowing.

secrets.name: The Count by the Sap
secrets.prompt: Look at the count cut in the root wall
secrets.text: Cut in the root wall across from the glowing pool, notches by the hundred in rows of five: the Keepers who came down to sit with the Root-Mother, one cut each, the oldest grown over with bark.
secrets.clue: Down where the sap pools and glows, the root wall across from it is cut with a count in fives, the oldest grown over.
secrets.hint: Willow-Whisper says every Keeper who goes down to sit with the Root-Mother cuts one mark by the sap pool. There are more marks than Keepers now. Nobody says that part aloud.
secrets.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Root-Mother and the Veridian Keepers are CANON (book3); the count is GAME-ONLY.

secrets.name: Where Lichen-Still Sleeps
secrets.prompt: Read the stone in the root
secrets.text: On the east side of the deepest chamber, a stone set into the root and the root grown round it like a hand: LICHEN-STILL, WHO STAYED WHEN THE COLD CAME IN. Moss-lamps have been left on it, and one is still lit.
secrets.clue: At the very bottom, where the great root sits, a stone has been taken into the root like a hand closing. One lamp on it is still lit.
secrets.hint: Reed-Song says Lichen-Still stayed down at the bottom with the Root-Mother when the cold first came into the root. The root took the stone in. Somebody still leaves lamps.
secrets.canonStatus: PROVISIONAL foreshadowing within CANON: the Root-Mother and the cold in the root (book3 ch.6-7); Lichen-Still and the stone are GAME-ONLY.
